description:
This video was made possible thanks to everyone on the Simple History Patreon: https://www.patreon.com/simplehistory

The transcript explains why the red cross insignia became dangerous in the Pacific Theater of WWII and beyond. It says combat medics were considered non-combatants in theory, but enemies targeted them anyway—specifically noting that the Japanese targeted medics because their deaths would cripple American morale. After that, medics stopped wearing identifiable symbols, and after WWII the transcript adds that the Viet Cong and NVA also targeted medics, leading armbands and painted helmets to be put aside; even medevac helicopters painted with red crosses became targets, so the crosses were painted over and gunships escorted flights. What other battlefield-protection myths should we cover next?

title: Why the Red Cross Became a Target in WWII
